modules.name: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

blocks.title: Example
blocks.question:
Which of the following compounds is expected to have the highest boiling point?

(a) Butane

(b) Pentane

(c) Propan-1-ol

(d) Diethyl ether
blocks.answer:
Ans: Answer: c) Propan-1-ol

Explanation: Propan-1-ol has the highest boiling point among the given options. This is because alcohols can form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds due to the presence of the polar -OH group. A significant amount of energy is required to overcome these forces. In contrast, butane and pentane (alkanes) only have weak van der Waals forces, and diethyl ether, while polar, cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself. Therefore, alcohols have considerably higher boiling points than hydrocarbons and ethers of comparable molecular masses.

blocks.title: Example-1
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement-I: In ether formation by Williamson synthesis, if a primary alkyl halide is used, an alkene is the only reaction product and no ether is formed.

Statement-II: Alkoxides are not only nucleophiles but strong bases as well. They react with alkyl halides, leading to elimination reactions as well as substitution reactions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

(1) Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

(2) Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct

(3) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

(4) Both statements I and statements II are correct
blocks.answer:
Answer: (2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Explanation:

  • Statement I: Incorrect
In the Williamson synthesis, if a primary alkyl halide is used, the reaction proceeds via an SN2 mechanism, leading to the formation of an ether. No alkene is formed unless the alkyl halide is hindered or secondary/tertiary.
  • Statement II: Correct
Alkoxides ($RO^-$) are both strong nucleophiles and strong bases. They can participate in nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reactions to form ethers, and in elimination (E2) reactions, leading to alkenes depending on the reaction conditions and the nature of the alkyl halide.

(4) Both statements I and statements II are correct

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question:
On the reaction of ether with BF3 ether act as

(1) Electrophile

(2) Nucleophile

(3) Ambiphile

(4) None
blocks.answer:
Answer: (2) Nucleophile

In the reaction of an ether with BF₃ (boron trifluoride), the ether acts as a nucleophile. This is because the oxygen atom in the ether molecule has lone pairs of electrons, which can donate electrons to the electron-deficient boron atom in BF₃, forming a coordinate bond.

BF₃ is a Lewis acid, and the ether behaves as a Lewis base (nucleophile) in this interaction.
